prompt.title: Trello board operating map
prompt.instructions: Use this map to operate a user-authorized Trello board through the visible UI only. Read the adjacent SKILL.md before mutating a board. Act like a careful productivity assistant: first read the board with portable actions.site operations, then ask clarifying questions when the requested outcome is ambiguous, then use the smallest safe visible-UI operation and verify it. Prefer Trello-specific executable read, candidate, scroll, and interaction actions over generic DOM observation or direct primitive fallback calls. Some older entries are workflow recipes, not reliable hosted-agent mutations; if an action output or description says recipe, guidance, executable:false, or verification_required, do not claim a mutation from that call. Instead follow the named executable Trello actions step by step. If a requested card or list appears in the board text but is not returned as a visible candidate, treat it as horizontally offscreen inside the Trello board region and call trello.board.scroll_left or trello.board.scroll_right before retrying the Trello-specific action; use trello.board.scroll_horizontal only when a specific signed delta is needed. If the current tab URL is already a Trello /c/ card route, do not reopen the same card by title before using card-modal controls; first try the modal controls directly and verify Labels, Dates, or Checklist are visible. Before board-level mutations such as adding a card to a list, moving cards, or scrolling columns, call trello.card.close if a card route/modal is open, then verify the board route is active. To inspect an open card, prefer trello.card.detail.read over trello.card.modal_text.read. trello.card.detail.read is the low-token card-state projection: it exposes title, list, labels, description surface, due date surface, checklist sections/items, comments/activity controls, visible counts, and partial-state warnings. Use trello.card.modal_text.read only as a fallback smoke test that a card modal exists; it can truncate long card content and must not be used to enumerate checklists. After creating or updating a card, verification must bind the exact target identity: the exact card title, source URL when provenance matters, and expected list if list placement matters. Do not claim verification from a generic board/list projection unless that projection output contains the target title and expected source/list. If the target list or card is not present in the verification output, call trello.card.by_title.open with the exact title or scroll/read until the target appears; otherwise report that verification is incomplete. If trello.card.detail.read shows only the first checklist rows, call trello.card.content.scroll with a positive delta_y, then call trello.card.detail.read again; Trello scrolls the card's left main pane, not the modal, checklist UL, or page viewport. To open a visible card, call trello.board.visible_card_surfaces.candidates, select the candidate whose text contains the exact requested title, click it with trello.interaction.pointer.click, then verify with trello.card.detail.read. To move a card between Trello board lists, open the card and prefer trello.card.move_to_list_from_open_card with the exact card title and target list. That action uses the current reliable route: Actions > Move, dismiss any Jira spotlight, filter Trello's React-select List field by the target list, select the matching option, and submit. The older current-list button and move-dialog candidate actions are diagnostic only on current Trello because the old popover selector can return no options. Never claim a move until the trello.board projection shows the target card under the target list. To reorder Trello lists, prefer trello.board.list.move_to_position with the exact source list name and one-based target position. It scans horizontally for the named list, opens that list's menu, uses Trello's Move list dialog, selects the numeric Position option, submits, and returns a verification requirement. Do not compose list reordering from broad list_headings/list_menu candidate reads; those projections are viewport diagnostics and may not identify an offscreen named list. Never type into the Move list Position combobox; Trello can display the typed number without selecting a valid option. If the actions.json overlay or menu host blocks Trello popover items, close the overlay before retrying. Do not claim list reordering from pointer.drag unless the postcondition read proves the new order. Do not use current-list or move-dialog actions for checklist tasks. A checklist is card content, not a Trello board list. To create a checklist or checklist item, do not rely on workflow-only checklist recipes. Use trello.card.add_menu_button.candidates, trello.card.add_menu_items.candidates, trello.card.checklist_title_inputs.candidates, trello.card.checklist_submit_buttons.candidates, trello.card.checklist_item_controls.candidates, trello.card.checklist_item_inputs.candidates, trello.card.checklist_item_submit_buttons.candidates, and Trello interaction actions. For an existing checklist item, first click the exact Add an item control from trello.card.checklist_item_controls.candidates, then resolve the checklist item input, insert text, submit, and verify. To mark a checklist item done, use trello.card.checklist_unchecked_items.read first whenever the user gives a semantic phrase such as next unfinished item, matching validation, the relevant checklist item, or anything other than the exact checklist text. Copy the exact returned unchecked item text into trello.card.checklist_item.complete. Never invent or paraphrase item_text. Validation checklist items are evidence gates: only complete one after the underlying requested operation has succeeded and a board/card projection proves the requested outcome. If an import, movement, date change, label change, or other validation task could not be performed or verified, do not call trello.card.checklist_item.complete for that validation item; report the blocker and leave it unchecked. For Linear or LinkedIn transfer-buffer import validations, provenance is mandatory: the source item must come from an authorized Linear/LinkedIn source surface, transfer buffer, source URL, issue key, or copied source payload. For cross-tab transfer tasks, never decide that a Linear or LinkedIn source action is unavailable from the Trello catalog alone. First call browser.claimed_tabs.list, activate the claimed source tab, call actions.site mode=list on that source tab, and use source-site actions such as linear.issue.by_key.open and linear.issue.detail.read when available. Only report the source body unavailable after checking the source tab catalog and attempting the relevant source projection. A Trello card whose title merely contains words such as Linear, LinkedIn, or linear.app is not import evidence and must not satisfy the validation. If a validation item was checked by mistake, use trello.card.checklist_item.uncomplete with the exact item text to restore the evidence gate. If the task required opening or creating another card, return to the checklist-owner card first, usually with trello.card.by_title.open for that card title, then read unchecked items and call trello.card.checklist_item.complete with the exact item text. Do not infer completion merely because item text is visible. Verify with trello.card.detail.read or trello.card_modal state that the exact item has aria_checked true. Verify with trello.card.detail.read and require the exact checklist title, item text, or checked state before claiming success. For labels, due dates, and descriptions, use the named Trello candidate actions for the relevant popover/editor and verify with card detail or visible board/list reads before claiming success. For trello.card.description.set, inspect the returned value. If output.value.verified is false, the description update is not verified even when ok is true; for long Linear/LinkedIn imports pass verify_contains as a short distinctive URL-free body phrase (the comparison is whitespace-normalized, so newlines in the sentinel are fine; never put a raw URL in the sentinel because Trello renders URLs as titled smart links and the raw URL text vanishes from the modal). Verify the source URL separately with trello.card.description_links.read by matching the href values. If verified is false, re-check with trello.card.modal_text.read using a shorter sentinel; do not re-run trello.card.description.set unless the content is genuinely absent, because re-setting overwrites the saved description and destroys its formatting. For requested due dates, every requested component is mandatory: resolve relative dates to a concrete calendar day, set the requested time when provided, stop immediately if any date sub-action fails, and do not save, report success, or complete a validation checklist item unless the final visible card state contains the exact requested date and time. Never treat a generic date badge as proof of a specific requested date/time. Never use Trello private/internal REST APIs or debugger-backed actions for user-account operations. For GPT Realtime validation, every mutation and verification step must be executable through portable actions.json primitives. End every card task at the base state: after finishing operations on a card, close it with trello.card.close and leave the user looking at the plain board view — never leave a card modal, popover, composer, or side panel (such as Planner) dominating the view — unless the user explicitly asked to keep the card open. Destructiveness never escalates: archive and delete are different operations — when the user says archive, call trello.card.archive (recoverable), never trello.card.delete (permanent); report the exact operation you performed. The base state includes side panels: when a task ends or the user asks for a clean view, close side panels that were opened as a side effect of your own work (use trello.board.planner.close for the Planner) and confirm with the action output that the panel is actually gone. Never close a panel the user opened deliberately or is actively using — if the user is exploring a panel such as Planner, help them use it instead. ACCESSIBILITY NAVIGATION (use these — they are the reliable way to find controls): the extension exposes accessibility primitives that resolve a control by its ROLE and ACCESSIBLE NAME and return its exact clickable center — far more reliable than pixel coordinates or generic DOM hunting. When you need to click a Trello control that a Trello-specific action does not already cover (e.g. the top-nav 'Create' button, a 'Create board' menu item, a board-menu entry, 'Add a card', 'Add another list', a 'Save'/'Create' submit button, the board-menu '...' button): call a11y.query with {role, name} or {role, name_contains} to get its clickable_center, then pointer.click that center. Use a11y.tree to see the board's structural outline (lists, buttons, menu items) when you are unsure what is on screen or what a control is called. Order of preference for any interaction: (1) a Trello-specific action from this map; (2) a11y.query/a11y.tree to resolve the control by identity, then pointer.click; (3) only then generic DOM/coordinate fallback. Prefer a11y identity resolution over screenshot pixel-guessing — it does not break when the layout shifts.
prompt.state_summary: Live validation on extension 0.1.104 proved visible To Do card creation, offscreen card recovery, GPT Realtime card movement through the Move dialog, checklist item insertion, label application, due-date setting, description editing, list creation, and list reordering through Trello's Move list dialog using executable candidate actions plus pointer/text/keyboard primitives. The remaining gaps are Calendar enablement and Linear/LinkedIn imports.

tools.name: trello.card.drag_between_lists
tools.description: Move a card from one list to another by a REAL animated drag (visible card-follows-cursor motion), then VERIFY the move by structured list-membership read. Use when the user wants the card physically dragged between columns (not the Actions>Move menu). Resolves the card and destination list by identity-bearing locators at dispatch time, so the pointer.drag runtime can attest that both points are visible and receive events before emitting a drag. Performs an animated trusted pointer.drag (duration_ms for the visible glide), and — because pointer.drag can report event-success without moving the card — REQUIRES a post-drag verification: the card title must appear under destination_list_name and must NOT remain under source_list_name. Fails loudly (ok:false) if verification does not confirm the move; never claims success on drag-event success alone.

card_title.description: Exact visible title of the card to drag.

source_list_name.description: List the card is currently in.

destination_list_name.description: List to drag the card into.

duration_ms.description: Animated drag duration; 600ms gives a visible glide. 0 = instant.

workflow.output: {% ( $dragReady := $exists(steps.findCard.output.clickable_center.x) and $exists(steps.findDestList.output.clickable_center.x); {'drag_ready': $dragReady, 'dragged': steps.animatedDrag.output.dragged, 'fidelity': steps.animatedDrag.output.fidelity, 'card_title': input.card_title, 'source_list_name': input.source_list_name, 'destination_list_name': input.destination_list_name, 'verification_required': 'Call actions.site state_read projection trello.board and verify card_title appears under destination_list_name and not under source_list_name.', 'next_step': $dragReady ? 'Drag dispatched; independently verify the card moved.' : 'Card or destination coordinates were not resolved; no drag was dispatched. Re-read the board and retry only after both targets are resolved.'} ) %}

source.why: Promoted from the private Trello map after the private map listed actions that actions.site could not dispatch. Uses trusted pointer.drag when available and returns the board projection for caller-side postcondition verification.

x_actions.validation_note: pointer.drag can return event-dispatch success without moving the card (live 2026-06-10). Post-drag trello.board verification is MANDATORY; this action is not successful on drag-event success alone.

tools.name: trello.board.list_headings.candidates
tools.description: Resolve all visible Trello list headings to text and viewport geometry. Use this before adding a card to a named list: choose the heading whose text matches the requested list, then pair it with the Add a card button in the same column from trello.board.add_card_buttons.candidates. Use the ordered candidates to verify visible list order after list creation or reordering. This avoids broad generic DOM reads.

source.why: List-name geometry lets the agent associate list-specific controls by column position without querying the whole page for generic words such as Card.

tools.name: trello.board.list_wrappers.candidates
tools.description: Resolve visible Trello list wrapper containers to text and viewport geometry. Use this to inspect list order and geometry. Do not prefer wrapper drag for list reordering: live validation showed Trello can ignore pointer.drag even when the primitive reports dragged:true. Prefer the list menu Move list dialog actions for list reordering, then verify the new order with trello.board.list_headings.candidates or trello.board.visible_lists.read.

source.why: List reordering failed when the hosted agent dragged heading centers. Trello needs container/header-band geometry and a left-edge drop target for reliable horizontal list reorder gestures.

tools.name: trello.board.list_menu_buttons.candidates
tools.description: Resolve visible Trello list action-menu buttons. Match the source list by the button text or aria-label such as 'More actions on Validation List 0926'. Use this before list-level operations such as Move list. If an actions.json overlay blocks the Trello popover after opening the menu, close the overlay and retry.

source.why: Trello list reordering is more reliable through the visible list menu Move list dialog than synthetic horizontal drag.

tools.name: trello.board.list_menu_by_name.open
tools.description: Open the actions menu for a named Trello list, even when the list starts horizontally offscreen. This is the preferred setup action for list-level operations. It closes an open card modal if present, hides the actions.json overlay, resets to the board start, scans right for the exact list heading, retargets through that list wrapper to its real menu button, and verifies the list actions popover opened.

source.why: Hosted GPT could not operate an offscreen list because broad list-heading/menu projections only exposed the currently visible or auto-scrolled first list. This action targets a named list wrapper and lets locator.element_info scroll that one target into view before clicking its menu.

tools.name: trello.board.list.move_to_position
tools.description: Move a named Trello list to a one-based board position using the visible Move list dialog. Use this for natural requests like moving a list one slot left/right after computing the target position from the current board order. Never type the position; this action opens the Position dropdown and clicks the numeric option. After it returns, verify board order with trello.board.visible_lists.read or the Trello board state projection before claiming success.

list_name.description: Exact Trello list name to move.

target_position.description: One-based Trello board position to select in the Move list dialog.

source.why: List reordering should be a named, parameter-bound state-machine action. Broad visible candidate projections were too fragile because locator.element_info auto-scrolled the first rendered list back into view and caused the agent to ask the human to scroll.

tools.name: trello.board.move_list_position_inputs.candidates
tools.description: Resolve the tiny hidden combobox inputs inside the Trello Move list popover. This is diagnostic only: do not click these tiny input centers and never use trello.interaction.text.insert to type a position. Use trello.board.move_list_position_boxes.candidates instead, then select a numeric option.

source.selector_notes: Trello renders the Board and Position custom selects as narrow hidden inputs. Hosted GPT failed by typing into this input; use the larger visible boxes action instead.

tools.name: trello.board.move_list_position_boxes.candidates
tools.description: Resolve the two visible custom-select boxes inside the Trello Move list popover. This action should return exactly two candidates: first Board, second Position. To open Position, click the center of the second candidate, then press ArrowDown with trello.interaction.keyboard.press, then call trello.board.move_list_position_options.candidates. Never type into the Position combobox; click an option candidate instead. If this action returns more or fewer than two candidates, do not click Move; reopen the popover and retry.

source.why: The visible Trello custom-select boxes have usable geometry, while their child combobox inputs are only a few pixels wide and invite invalid text insertion. The adjacent-sibling selector returns the two clickable visible boxes directly; the previous direct-child :has selector failed because Trello nests the combobox input deeper.

tools.name: trello.board.move_list_position_options.candidates
tools.description: Resolve numeric position options after the Move list Position box is open. If no options are visible after clicking the Position box, press ArrowDown and retry this action. Click an option candidate; do not type the number with text.insert. The option numbers are full-board one-based list positions, not just visible-candidate indexes. If the Move popover currently shows source Position 7 and the user asks to move the source immediately before the previous adjacent list, choose option 6, click Move, then verify ordered headings.

source.why: Trello's Move-list Position control did not expose [role='option'] elements. After focusing the Position box and pressing ArrowDown, the numeric options appeared as React-select option divs with ids containing react-select and option.

tools.name: trello.board.move_list_submit_button.candidates

source.why: A flat card read cannot prove list membership after movement. Returning one text block per visible list gives agents a durable postcondition without using debugger JavaScript or Trello APIs.

tools.name: trello.card.delete
tools.description:
PERMANENTLY delete the currently open Trello card — unrecoverable. Use ONLY when the user explicitly says delete permanently. When the user says archive, remove, or clean up, use trello.card.archive instead. Never escalate an archive request into a delete, and report the exact operation performed (archived vs deleted) in your answer.

THE REAL FLOW, measured live 2026-07-10 on a throwaway card. Trello has no direct delete: Actions > Archive, and only THEN does the card grow a banner with Restore + Delete.

  card-back-actions-button   exists, labelled 'Actions'   -> opens a role=dialog
  card-back-archive-button   exists ONLY once that menu is open
  card-back-delete-card-button   appears ONLY after archiving

Do not scope this workflow to [data-testid='popover']; that selector matches zero elements in the live delete flow. The permanent Delete button is [data-testid='card-back-delete-card-button']; the final confirm is [data-testid='popover-confirm-button']. Verify by card modal absence and then by the trello.board projection.

workflow.output: {% { 'deleted_card': $exists(input.title) ? input.title : 'open card', 'card_back_still_open': steps.verifyCardGone.output.match_count > 0, 'deleted': steps.verifyCardGone.output.match_count = 0, 'verification_required': 'deleted:true means no card-back remains (verifyCardGone observed match_count 0). The step retries and HARD-FAILS (workflow_retry_exhausted) if the card is still open, so a successful call already proves the delete. Confirm via the trello.board projection.' } %}

source.why: Archive-then-delete flow discovered live 2026-06-12 on the open card actions menu (aria-label matches ction/enu, distinct from the lose close button); after Archive the same menu offers Delete, then a full-width confirm Delete follows. Destructive: guarded by description; only runs against an explicitly opened card.

tools.name: trello.list.rename
tools.description: Rename a Trello list by inline-editing its header. AUTHORED BY THE HOSTED AGENT (PR #7, 2026-07-04) from a live exploration, review-hardened on promotion. Structure discovered live: every list header contains an ALWAYS-PRESENT textarea[data-testid='list-name-textarea'] whose aria-label is the list name, overlaid by the visible h2[data-testid='list-name']; clicking the h2 focuses that textarea (observed focused:true). tools.name: trello.card.due_date.recipe
tools.description: DO NOT CALL THIS ACTION DIRECTLY — it has no workflow and will return unsupported_execution_mode. It is a RECIPE you READ, then execute by calling the small sub-actions in order: trello.card.by_title.open, trello.card.date_popover.open, trello.card.date_popover.page_to_month, trello.card.date_popover.pick_day, optionally trello.card.date_popover.set_time, then trello.card.date_popover.save. set a Trello card's due date by composing the small date actions, verifying each step. Resolve relative phrasing (next Friday) to a concrete date FIRST. Steps: (1) trello.card.by_title.open with the card title; verify the card modal opened. (2) trello.card.date_popover.open; verify the popover/month header is visible. (3) trello.card.date_popover.page_to_month with month_year '<Month> <Year>'; verify the header matches. (4) trello.card.date_popover.pick_day with day_button_label '<day>, <Weekday> <Month> <Year>'. (5) optionally trello.card.date_popover.set_time with 'H:MM AM/PM'. (6) trello.card.date_popover.save. Then confirm with the trello.board projection due_date field (state_read or state_diff). Each sub-action is one primitive-free actions.site call; calling them in order is NOT resorting to primitives. Prefer this recipe over a giant single workflow: each step is independently verifiable and recoverable. Requires the spec-026 settle_after workflow engine (extension 0.1.109+).

card_title.description: Distinctive visible text from the Trello card title to receive the due date.

day_button_label.description: The target calendar day's full aria-label exactly as Trello renders it: '<day>, <Weekday> <Month> <Year>', for example '20, Saturday June 2026'. Compute the weekday for the concrete date before calling.

month_year.description: The target month and year as shown in the calendar header, '<Month> <Year>', for example 'June 2026'. Used to page the calendar to the correct month before clicking the day.

time.description: Optional time of day in 'H:MM AM/PM' format, for example '2:30 PM'. Omit to leave Trello's default due time.

source.why: Agent-sequenced recipe composing the small date actions (by_title.open -> date_popover.open -> page_to_month -> pick_day -> [set_time] -> save). Replaces the monolithic single-call workflow, which was timing-fragile across the popover-open/page-to-month boundary. Each sub-action is independently testable and recoverable; the agent verifies each step.

tools.name: trello.card.description.set
tools.description: Set the description on a specifically named, currently open Trello card with no agent primitives: verify the open card title, open the description editor, atomically replace its contents, save, and verify a distinctive substring on the saved description surface. Precondition: open the intended card first with trello.card.by_title.open, then pass that exact card title as card_title. For long descriptions, pass verify_contains as a short distinctive URL-free body phrase; the comparison is whitespace-normalized, so sentinels may contain newlines. Do not claim success unless output.verified is true. If verified is false, re-check with trello.card.detail.read and a shorter sentinel before anything else; only re-run this action if the content is genuinely absent, because re-setting overwrites the saved description and its formatting. IMPORTANT: verify_contains must not include raw URLs — Trello converts pasted URLs into titled smart links, so the raw URL text disappears from the visible description. Verify URLs separately with trello.card.description_links.read (href match). CRM boards: user-stated facts (meeting outcomes, decisions, next actions) must be captured here at the moment they are said — the card is the system of record, not the conversation. FORMATTING: write multi-line text — separate sections with blank lines (\n\n) and start bullet lines with '- '. Never write the whole description as one long line; that renders as an unreadable wall of text. tools.name: trello.card.title.set

Opens the card briefly, replaces the title in the card-back title field, commits with a trusted Enter, closes the card, and verifies the exact new title on the same stable Trello card ID captured before mutation. The open editor's aria-label is a transient editor signal and is diagnostic only; Trello can persist the rename before that attribute settles, so persisted board-front identity is the authoritative in-action verifier. Destination-title duplicates are safe because verification is bound to the original card ID, not merely to any card with the requested title. BOARD CONVENTION: card titles are the person's name ONLY; context such as 'a company/context tag' belongs in the description or a label, never repeated in every title. Pass the card's exact current title as current_title and the desired title as new_title. The workflow scrolls to find the card automatically. Exact duplicate current titles are ambiguous and outside the measured boundary; resolve the intended card manually rather than calling this title-only action. If it fails with target_not_found on findCardFront, the card may ALREADY be renamed — re-read the board before retrying. HISTORICAL MEASURED BOUNDARY (2026-07-13, extension 0.1.206): six consecutive renames persisted on one disposable card, and an independent board projection proved the exact new title present and old title absent after every call. CURRENT COMMIT BOUNDARY (2026-07-16, extension 0.1.231): synthetic Enter updated the textarea and Trello's React value but left the persisted card title unchanged; trusted Enter persisted the exact new title. A transient editor aria-label retry then produced a false workflow failure even though an independent card lookup proved the exact new title present and the old title absent. Do not claim success unless output.verified is true, then independently confirm the exact new title is present and the old title is absent with the Trello board projection. After verified:false, re-read state before any retry.

tools.name: trello.card.checklist.read
tools.description:
PROJECTION - read the open Trello card's checklist state. Returns every mounted item's name and real checked state. Derive unchecked items by filtering items where checked=false; the projection intentionally does not duplicate every unchecked title in a second array because long checklists must stay within the workflow expression budget. Card-wide complete and percent_complete are derived from that same card-wide item state, so a section-local badge cannot contradict the returned items. section_percentages preserves every Trello checklist badge as diagnostic data. An empty checklist does not override checked items in another section; a card with no checklist items is not complete. Takes no arguments; reads whatever card is open (open it first with trello.card.by_title.open).

Requires extension >= 0.1.196. On older runtimes the workflow is rejected at parse time - invalid_workflow, unknown primitive dom.observe.attributes - before any step runs.

HISTORY, so nobody re-derives the wrong fixes. This once returned an empty item list because dom.observe.visible filtered rows outside the viewport; dom.observe.attributes now enumerates mounted rows without that filter. It later combined those card-wide rows with one section-local percentage, producing complete:false with every returned item checked when an empty checklist came first. Completion now uses one card-wide authority and section percentages remain separate diagnostics. A 59-item checklist later exceeded the 16 KB JSONata expression budget because unchecked titles were emitted twice; the compact items array is now the single authority. If Trello genuinely virtualizes unmounted checklist rows, treat item coverage as partial rather than inferring absence.

Always verify the returned incomplete field and then read trello.card.checklist.read to prove the exact item is unchecked before claiming success. Duplicate labels, paraphrased text, and larger virtualized checklists remain outside the measured boundary.

item_text.description: Exact checked checklist item text to mark incomplete.

workflow.output: {% ($t := input.item_text; {'item': $t, 'incomplete': $count(steps.verifyDesiredState.output.matches[attributes.`aria-label` = $t and attributes.`aria-checked` = 'false']) = 1, 'already_desired': $count(steps.readStateBefore.output.matches[attributes.`aria-label` = $t and attributes.`aria-checked` = 'false']) = 1, 'ambiguous': steps.resolveExactIdentity.output.ambiguous}) %}

postcondition.failure_message: The exact Trello checklist item was still checked after the uncomplete workflow.

source.why: 2026-07-09: findItemRow bound [data-testid='check-item-container']:has([data-testid='check-item-name']) with text_contains. Measured live on a 9-item checklist: 9 rows match check-item-container, ZERO match the :has() because check-item-name exists nowhere, every row's textContent is "", and the item text appears in NO element on the page (searched all of document.querySelectorAll('*')). Trello keeps the name only as the input's aria-label -- the accessible name a screen reader would announce. resolveLocatorCandidates searches textContent+aria-label+title+value, so a read on the input matches by item text. The blind agent's path and the blind human's path are the same element.

tools.name: trello.board.scroll_horizontal
tools.description: Scroll the Trello board list region horizontally by a signed delta. Prefer trello.board.scroll_left or trello.board.scroll_right for simple recovery; use this parameterized workflow when a specific delta is needed.

delta_x.description: Horizontal scroll amount for the Trello lists region. Negative scrolls left; positive scrolls right.

delta_y.description: Usually 0 for Trello board horizontal movement.

workflow.output: {% {'delta_x': input.delta_x, 'delta_y': input.delta_y ? input.delta_y : 0, 'scroll': steps.scrollBoard.output} %}

tools.name: trello.board.text_snapshot.read
tools.description: Read compact text from the Trello board region for verification and offscreen diagnosis. Use it to determine whether a list or card exists in the mounted board even when visible candidate extraction only returns currently visible columns.

source.why: Visible structured extraction only returns visible columns. The board text snapshot helps detect horizontally offscreen lists/cards and verify rough ordering after mutations.

tools.name: trello.card.modal_text.read
tools.description: Read compact text from the currently open Trello card modal ONLY. Use this after opening a card to verify that card controls such as Labels, Dates, Checklist, Description, comments, and activity are actually visible before mutating the card. If NO card modal is open, this returns target_not_found (it does NOT fall back to the whole page body) — that is the correct signal to open a card first, not evidence the page is broken. Do not interpret a not-found result here as a Trello load error.

source.why: trello.card.by_title.open can report click success even when the card modal is not the resulting active state. This read gives the agent a postcondition check. The previous selector included a 'body' fallback, which scraped Trello's hidden noscript 'please enable JavaScript' boilerplate whenever no modal was open, causing hosted agents to wrongly conclude the page was broken and abort. Scoped to the actual card modal so a missing modal returns a clean not-found instead of a misleading load-error string.

tools.name: trello.card.detail.read
tools.description: Read the currently open Trello card as structured, low-token card state. Prefer this over trello.card.modal_text.read whenever the agent needs to understand an opened card. It returns card title/list controls, labels, due/date controls, description surfaces, checklist title/progress/items, comments/activity controls, and coverage metadata. If the checklist item count looks lower than the visible Trello progress count, treat the result as partial and do not claim all checklist items were read. CRM CAPTURE DISCIPLINE: when the user tells you facts about the person on a card (meeting outcome, decision, next action), persist them to that card with trello.card.description.set IMMEDIATELY — before asking your next question or continuing the conversation. A verbal acknowledgment is not capture; the Trello card is the system of record.

arguments.item_selector: [data-testid='card-back-title-input'], [aria-label*='currently in' i], [data-testid='card-label'], [data-testid='card-back-due-date-button'], [data-testid='description-button'], [data-testid='checklist-container'], [data-testid='checklist-section'], [data-testid='checklist-title'], [data-testid='checklist-progress-percentage'], [data-testid='checklist-items'], [data-testid='check-item-container'], [data-testid='check-item-name'], [data-testid='clickable-checkbox'], input[type='checkbox'][aria-label], [data-testid='show-details-button'], [data-testid='card-back-activity-button'], [role='checkbox'], textarea, button, a[href*='/c/']

source.why: Hosted GPT Realtime failed to enumerate the demo-readiness checklist because trello.card.modal_text.read returned a truncated flattened modal blob. This action gives the model a focused card-state projection and exposes checklist row aria labels separately when Trello mounts them.
source.coverage_rule: This projection reports only mounted/visible Trello card elements. If a checklist progress indicator or user request implies more checklist items than returned rows, the agent must report partial coverage and use a dedicated reveal/scroll action before claiming full coverage.

tools.name: trello.card.content.scroll
tools.description: Scroll the left content pane of the currently open Trello card. Use this when trello.card.detail.read sees only the first rows of a checklist, description, or card body. Trello card routes scroll the left main pane; scrolling the modal, the checklist list, or the page viewport may report no movement and will not reveal hidden card content.

delta_y.description: Vertical scroll delta. Positive reveals lower card content; negative returns toward the card title.

workflow.output: {% {'delta_y': input.delta_y ? input.delta_y : 500, 'scroll': steps.scrollCardMain.output, 'card_text_after_scroll': steps.readCardAfterScroll.output.text, 'verification_required': 'Call trello.card.detail.read after scrolling and verify the requested card content is visible.'} %}

source.why: The demo-readiness checklist initially exposed only four rows. Live discovery showed the scrollable element is the card route left main pane, not the modal container, checklist UL, or page viewport.

tools.name: trello.card.visible_buttons.candidates
tools.description: Resolve visible button candidates on the open Trello card route or modal, including current-list, Add, Labels, Dates, Checklist, and popover buttons. Use this to choose exact modal controls by text and geometry before mutating a card.

source.why: Trello card routes reuse generic button text and can leave board controls visible behind the modal. Returning all visible button candidates lets the agent distinguish modal controls from board controls by text and geometry.

tools.name: trello.card.current_list_button.candidates
tools.description: Return visible current-list button candidates on an open Trello card for moving the card between Trello board lists only. Do not use this for checklist tasks; a checklist is card content, not a board list. To open the Move dialog for an explicit card movement request, choose the small top-left card-header/list button whose geometry is near the upper-left of the card route/modal, usually bounding_box.left < 170 and bounding_box.top < 110, then click it with trello.interaction.pointer.click. Verify the Move dialog opened by calling trello.card.move_dialog.list_options.candidates.

source.why: Manual validation showed clicking the card's current-list button opens Trello's Move card dialog. Exposing this as a named Trello action keeps the agent on the actions.json path.

tools.name: trello.card.move_dialog.list_options.candidates
tools.description: Return visible list-option candidates only from Trello's open Move card popover. Current Trello uses React-select controls, so this candidate action is diagnostic only; prefer trello.card.move_to_list_from_open_card for reliable movement. Choose a candidate only when its text exactly equals the target list. If no exact target-list candidate is returned, the Move popover is not open, the list combobox has not been filtered, or the target list is unavailable. Do not click current-list badges, Add, Checklist, Members, Labels, or other ordinary card controls as substitutes. Verify afterward with the trello.board projection.

source.why: Hosted-agent validation moved a card from In Progress to To Do by opening the current-list button, selecting the target list option in the Move dialog, and verifying list membership. A 2026-06-15 GPT Realtime session showed the previous broad fallback selector returned ordinary card-modal buttons when the Move popover was not open, causing repeated clicks on the current-list badge instead of selecting Done. This action is intentionally scoped to the Move popover so missing popover state becomes visible instead of ambiguous.

tools.name: trello.card.move_to_list_from_open_card
tools.description: Move the currently open Trello card to a named board list through the visible card UI. Precondition: the target card is already open on a Trello card route/modal; pass card_title, source_list, and target_list. This uses Actions > Move, dismisses Trello's Jira spotlight if it appears, filters the Move dialog's List combobox, selects the exact option, clicks Move, reads the open card's committed current-list control, and closes the card back to the board route. output.moved is true only when that control names target_list; event dispatch alone never counts as success. From the restored board surface, the registered board-model postcondition requires card_title under target_list and absent from source_list.

card_title.description: Exact visible title of the currently open card, used for board projection verification.

source_list.description: Exact source list name. The board-model postcondition requires the card to be absent here after the move.

target_list.description: Exact visible destination list name, for example Next Up or In Progress.

workflow.output: {% {'card_title': input.card_title, 'source_list': input.source_list, 'target_list': input.target_list, 'moved': $exists(steps.verifyMovedList.output.clickable_center.x), 'committed_list_text': steps.verifyMovedList.output.text, 'returned_to_board': steps.verifyCardClosed.output.match_count = 0 and steps.verifyBoardRoute.output.matched, 'verification_required': 'The registered board postcondition confirms card_title under target_list and absent from source_list.'} %}

source.why: Hosted-agent movement failed because the older current-list opener/list-options path no longer exposed options. Current Trello routes reliable movement through Actions > Move and React-select list filtering, with final board projection verification.

tools.name: trello.card.label_openers.candidates
tools.description: Resolve visible Trello card label opener buttons. Use after verifying a card modal/route is open. Trello may show Labels on unlabeled cards or Add a label when labels already exist.

source.why: Covers both Labels and Add a label wording variants.

tools.name: trello.board.scroll_left
tools.description: Scroll the Trello board list region left toward Backlog and earlier workflow lists. Use when a target list/card exists in board text but visible candidate actions cannot resolve it. This action scrolls [data-testid='lists'], not the global page viewport.

tools.name: trello.board.scroll_right
tools.description: Scroll the Trello board list region right toward Done, Validation Temp, and later workflow lists. Use when a target list/card exists in board text but visible candidate actions cannot resolve it. This action scrolls [data-testid='lists'], not the global page viewport.

tools.name: trello.card.close_button.info
tools.description: Resolve the Close dialog button on an open Trello card route/modal. Use before board-level mutations when the tab is on a /c/ card URL; closing returns to the board route where list/card composer actions behave reliably.

tools.name: trello.card.description_links.read
tools.description: Read the links (anchor text and href) inside the currently open Trello card description. Use this to verify saved URLs: Trello renders raw URLs as titled smart links, so a pasted URL disappears from the visible modal text but remains as the anchor href. Verify source provenance (for example a Linear issue URL) by checking the href values returned here, never by searching modal text for the raw URL.

tools.name: trello.card.close
tools.description: Close the currently open Trello card modal and return to the plain board view. Call this after finishing operations on a card unless the user explicitly asked to keep the card open. Trello can place a nested dismissible surface inside the card, including an open checklist item composer; the workflow sends one Escape, probes whether the card is still open, and sends one conditional second Escape when the first only dismissed that nested surface. Verifies the modal is gone and the board lists are visible.

workflow.output: {% ( $boardVisible := $exists(steps.verifyBoardVisible.output.bounding_box); $cardGone := $not($exists(steps.verifyCardGone.output.bounding_box)); {'closed': $boardVisible and $cardGone, 'board_visible': $boardVisible, 'card_gone': $cardGone, 'next_step': ($boardVisible and $cardGone) ? 'Card modal closed and board view verified.' : 'Card modal closure was not verified; do not claim success or continue with board-level work.'} ) %}

tools.name: trello.card.archive
tools.description: Archive the currently open Trello card (recoverable — the card moves to the board archive) and return to the board view. Use this when the user asks to archive, remove, or clean up a card. Archiving is NOT deleting: never use trello.card.delete for an archive request, because delete is permanent and unrecoverable.

card_title.description: Exact title of the open card to archive.

workflow.output: {% { 'card': input.card_title, 'archived': $contains(steps.verifyArchived.output.text, 'This card was archived'), 'verified': $contains(steps.verifyArchived.output.text, 'This card was archived'), 'board_visible': $exists(steps.verifyBoardVisible.output.bounding_box), 'safe_to_claim': false, 'archive_banner_text': steps.verifyArchived.output.text, 'verification_required': 'verified:true means the exact open card exposed Trello archived-state text before the action returned to the board. safe_to_claim remains false until a separate board projection proves that the exact card left its list.' } %}

tools.description: Close the Trello Planner side panel if it is open, restoring the plain board view. The Planner is toggled by the left-nav Planner button; this action clicks it only when the panel is visible and verifies the panel is gone afterward.

The step retries and HARD-FAILS if the panel is still present.' } %}

Menu items include View calendars, Filter due cards shown, Add account, Upgrade, Disconnect account.

tools.description: Open the Planner settings menu, click View calendars, and read the connected Google account and the calendar list with per-calendar enabled state. Use this to answer which account is connected and which calendars are included in the Planner. The panel renders into an .atlaskit-portal-container at the document root. Leaves the calendars panel open so the user can tick checkboxes; the user closes it or presses Escape when done.

Checkbox states are not in the text — ask the user to tick calendars, or use locator reads per calendar label.'} %}

tools.name: trello.board.create
tools.description:
Create a NEW Trello board end to end with no agent primitives: open the top-nav Create menu, choose Create board, type the board name into the dialog's title field, and click the dialog's Create button. The new board opens (URL changes to /b/<id>/<slug>). Only the board title is required; Workspace and Visibility default. Verify by reading page.info (URL contains /b/) and the board title. Use this before adding lists or cards to a brand-new board.

⚠️ READINESS (2026-07-09): clickCreate's settle_after and findCreateBoardItem both bound a bare `button` + text_contains 'Create board'. MEASURED: the header trigger itself carries aria-label="Create board or Workspace", and resolveLocatorCandidates's haystack includes aria-label — so both resolved to THE BUTTON THEY JUST CLICKED. The settle satisfied instantly and proved nothing about whether the menu opened. A settle that matches its own trigger is worse than no settle. Both now bind [data-testid='header-create-board-button'] inside [data-testid='header-create-menu-popover']. Do NOT widen them back to `button`.

name.description: Exact title for the new board.

source.why: Lifts board creation from top-nav Create menu geometry plus manual typing to a single primitive-free workflow, so a new board (e.g. an Investigations board) can be created without hand-driven clicks.

workflow.output: {% {'created_board': input.name, 'url': steps.verify.output.url, 'on_board_route': $contains(steps.verify.output.url, '/b/')} %}

workflows.name: reset_board_to_tutorial_lists
workflows.description: Clear existing board lists and recreate the tutorial list set: Organize Me, To Do, On Hold, Doing, Done. Use only visible Trello UI controls.
steps: trello.board.visible_lists.read to inventory current lists
for each existing list: resolve the list header/menu button in the visible UI, open the list menu, choose Archive this list, and verify the list disappeared
trello.board.add_list_button.info
pointer.click
text.insert into [data-testid='list-name-textarea'] with the next list title
keyboard.press Enter or click Add list
verify each list appears in trello.board.visible_lists.read before creating the next list
workflows.safety: Do not use Trello REST/internal API endpoints. Ask for confirmation before archiving existing lists unless the user explicitly asked to reset the board.

workflows.name: create_card_in_named_list
workflows.description: Create a card with the given title in the named list.
steps: trello.board.visible_lists.read to locate the target list
scroll horizontally or vertically until the target list and its Add a card button are visible
call trello.board.list_headings.candidates and trello.board.add_card_buttons.candidates; choose the Add a card button whose column geometry aligns with the requested list heading
pointer.click
text.insert into [data-testid='list-card-composer-textarea']; this element is contenteditable and is not a textarea
keyboard.press Enter or click Add card
verify the card appears in the target list snapshot
known_traps: Do not type the card title into [data-testid='list-name-textarea']; that is the list composer.
Do not assume the first Add a card button belongs to the requested list.
Do not call dom.observe.visible with broad text such as Card; it can return a large ambiguous page payload and does not encode Trello list intent.
If the card is offscreen after creation, read the list snapshot rather than relying on the visible viewport only.

workflows.name: apply_or_create_label_on_card
workflows.description: Open a card by exact title, create a label when needed, and apply it to the card.
steps: trello.board.visible_cards.read to locate the card
scroll until the card is visible and use pointer.click on the exact card title
open the label popover by clicking Labels, or Add a label when labels already exist
if the label exists, click the matching label[data-testid='clickable-checkbox']
if the label does not exist, use Create a new label or edit an unused label color, type the title into #edit-label-title-input, choose the desired color, save, then select it
close the popover and verify the label badge appears on the card
known_traps: #edit-label-title-input is the validated label title input.
The global search input [data-testid='cross-product-search-input-skeleton'] is not the label title field.
After labels exist on a card, the visible control may read Add a label instead of Labels.

workflows.name: apply_priority_labels
workflows.description: Apply priority labels such as P0 and P1 to a set of cards.
steps: ensure labels P0 and P1 exist using apply_or_create_label_on_card
for each card title, open the card, open Labels or Add a label, select the priority label checkbox, close the modal or return to board
verify each target card shows the requested priority label badge

workflows.name: set_card_due_date
workflows.description: Set a Trello card due date by opening the date popover, choosing the calendar day, and saving.
steps: open the card by exact title
open the date editor by clicking Dates, or the existing due-date badge if a date is already set
prefer selecting the calendar day button by aria-label such as '10, Wednesday June 2026'
click [data-testid='save-date-button']
verify the due date badge appears on the card and in the board snapshot
known_traps: Typing into [data-testid='due-date-field'] did not reliably change the date during validation.
Calendar-day selection plus Save was the reliable path.
If the card already has a due date, the opener may no longer say Dates.

workflows.name: open_calendar_view
workflows.description: Open the Trello Calendar view and read the dated cards visible in the calendar.
steps: trello.board.views_button.info
pointer.click
trello.board.view_switcher.options.read
resolve the Calendar option, usually [data-testid='view-switcher-button-calendar'] or an href ending in /calendar-view
pointer.click on Calendar
verify the URL contains /calendar-view or the calendar wrapper is visible
trello.board.calendar_events.read
workflows.notes: On the validated board, Calendar was already available from Views. If Calendar is not available, use enable_calendar_power_up with user confirmation.

workflows.name: enable_calendar_power_up
workflows.description: Find the Calendar Power-Up from the board Power-Ups directory and enable it after explicit user confirmation.
steps: trello.board.show_menu_button.info or the board-header Power-Ups button
pointer.click to open the board menu or Power-Ups route
open Power-Ups
trello.board.power_ups_directory.read
locate the Calendar Power-Up tile by text 'Calendar Power-Up' and summary 'Visualize Trello cards in a calendar view'
ask for confirmation before clicking Add because this mutates board integration state
after confirmation, click the Add button associated with the Calendar Power-Up tile
return to the board and verify Calendar appears under Views
workflows.notes: The Power-Ups directory and Calendar Power-Up tile were live-validated. The final Add click was intentionally not executed during mapping because it changes board integration state.

workflows.name: build_goal_card_from_task_links
workflows.description: Create or open a goal card in Doing, add a checklist, and paste links to supporting task cards so the goal card organizes work under a daily goal.
steps: read the board snapshot and locate the supporting task cards
for each task card, open the exact card and copy its browser URL or card share link
create or open the goal card in Doing
click Checklist in the goal card modal
name the checklist if needed
add each copied task-card URL as a checklist item
verify Trello recognizes each URL as a useful card link
preserve task labels and due dates on the original task cards
archive original task cards only after the user confirms that linked goal checklists are the intended workflow

workflows.name: move_card_between_lists
workflows.description: Move a card from one list to another during review or while assisting a live meeting.
steps: read the board snapshot and verify the source card and destination list
scroll until both the card and a viable destination area are visible, or move in two safe viewport steps
drag the card from its visible card body to the destination list
verify the card title appears in the destination list and no duplicate remains in the source list
if the drag fails or target list is offscreen, stop and report the primitive limitation instead of pretending the move occurred
workflows.why_essential: A Trello meeting assistant must move cards while listening to a meeting: completed work to Done, deferred work to On Hold, active goals to Doing, and future goals to To Do.

workflows.name: daily_review_with_calendar_and_goals
workflows.description: Use the tutorial's daily review habit: inspect dated cards in Calendar, choose today's goals, organize supporting tasks under goal checklists, and move cards as work changes.
steps: open_calendar_view and read dated work
ask the user which outcomes matter today if priorities are ambiguous
choose one to three goal cards for Doing
for each goal, link supporting tasks in a checklist
move completed goals to Done
move unfinished low-priority goals to On Hold
capture newly discovered tasks in Organize Me
verify the board snapshot before ending the review

workflows.name: import_task_batch_to_board
workflows.description: Given a task list from another source, create cards in the appropriate Trello lists, apply category and priority labels, set due dates, and verify the result.
steps: read and verify the target Trello lists
create cards in small batches with create_card_in_named_list
verify the cards before applying labels
apply category labels and priority labels
set due dates through the calendar picker
run a board snapshot and compare expected cards, labels, and due dates against observed state
workflows.notes: The source extraction, such as reading Linear tasks, belongs to that source site's actions.json. This Trello workflow only consumes already-extracted task data.

files.description: UI-only Trello operating guidance for creating cards/lists, labels, due dates, goals, checklists, movement, and tutorial replication.

state_projections.name: trello.board
state_projections.description: Logical state of the visible Trello board: lists, cards, labels, due dates, and checklist summaries.

summaries.name: agent_context
summaries.description: Bounded board orientation: list counts plus small In Progress and Next previews. Use list_page for exhaustive list traversal.
summaries.expression: {% ( $lists := state.board.lists; $visibleLists := $filter($lists, function($list, $index) { $index < 25 }); $compactPreview := function($card) { {'title': $substring($card.title, 0, 180), 'labels': $count($card.labels) > 0 ? $append([], $map($filter($card.labels, function($label, $index) { $index < 3 }), function($label) { $substring($label.text ? $label.text : $label.name, 0, 40) })) : [], 'due_date': $card.due_date ? $substring($card.due_date, 0, 40) : null, 'checklist_summary': $card.checklist_summary ? $substring($card.checklist_summary, 0, 40) : null} }; $activeCards := state.board.lists[name = 'In Progress'][0].cards; $nextCards := state.board.lists[name = 'Next'][0].cards; {'list_count': $count($lists), 'total_card_count': $count($lists) > 0 ? $sum($lists.card_count) : 0, 'lists_returned': $count($visibleLists), 'lists_truncated': $count($lists) > 25, 'lists': $count($visibleLists) > 0 ? $append([], $map($visibleLists, function($list, $index) { {'index': $index, 'name': $substring($list.name, 0, 80), 'card_count': $list.card_count} })) : [], 'in_progress_preview': $count($activeCards) > 0 ? $append([], $map($filter($activeCards, function($card, $index) { $index < 3 }), $compactPreview)) : [], 'next_preview': $count($nextCards) > 0 ? $append([], $map($filter($nextCards, function($card, $index) { $index < 3 }), $compactPreview)) : [], 'read_more': {'list_catalog_summary_name': 'lists_page', 'list_cards_summary_name': 'list_page', 'list_cards_required_arguments': ['list_name'], 'list_cards_optional_arguments': ['list_occurrence', 'offset', 'limit'], 'max_list_limit': 25, 'max_card_limit': 10}} ) %}

summaries.name: lists_page
summaries.description: Read the board's list catalog in bounded pages so every list remains discoverable.

summaries.name: list_page
summaries.description: Read one named Trello list in bounded pages of at most ten compact cards.
summaries.expression: {% ( $occurrence := $exists($$.input.list_occurrence) ? $$.input.list_occurrence : 0; $matches := state.board.lists[name = $$.input.list_name]; $list := $matches[$occurrence]; $found := $exists($list); $offset := $exists($$.input.offset) ? $$.input.offset : 0; $limit := $exists($$.input.limit) ? $$.input.limit : 10; $cards := $found ? $list.cards : []; $page := $filter($cards, function($card, $index) { $index >= $offset and $index < $offset + $limit }); $compactCard := function($card) { {'title': $substring($card.title, 0, 300), 'url': $card.url ? $substring($card.url, 0, 500) : null, 'labels': $count($card.labels) > 0 ? $append([], $map($filter($card.labels, function($label, $index) { $index < 4 }), function($label) { $substring($label.text ? $label.text : $label.name, 0, 60) })) : [], 'due_date': $card.due_date ? $substring($card.due_date, 0, 60) : null, 'checklist_summary': $card.checklist_summary ? $substring($card.checklist_summary, 0, 60) : null} }; {'found': $found, 'list_name': $found ? $list.name : $$.input.list_name, 'list_occurrence': $occurrence, 'matching_list_count': $count($matches), 'offset': $offset, 'limit': $limit, 'total_count': $count($cards), 'returned_count': $count($page), 'has_more': $offset + $limit < $count($cards), 'next_offset': $offset + $limit < $count($cards) ? $offset + $limit : null, 'cards': $count($page) > 0 ? $append([], $map($page, $compactCard)) : []} ) %}
